pages.title: Horizon Measurers
pages.text: $(o)"A step is not east until an observer supplies east. Give the walker a frame, then the same mark may become right, forward, or return."$()$(br2)Their surviving notes describe direction as a relation to an observer. Player-relative frames preserve this approach.

pages.title: Gatherers Of Means
pages.text: $(o)"Do not ask which lantern is the middle lantern. Ask where all lanterns would agree to meet."$()$(br2)They used repeated observations to locate centers, a practice echoed by centroid theorems and future target queries.

pages.title: Boundary Builders
pages.text: $(o)"A wall is one answer to a boundary. The rule that names where a wall belongs is the more durable answer."$()$(br2)Their diagrams treat an area as a condition. Regions and anchors inherit that idea.

pages.title: Unfinished Notes
pages.text: Scattered manuscripts mention rotating gardens, paths that avoid fragile ground, and moving marks divided among many hands. These are $(thing)conjectures$(), not available spells yet.$(br2)When a conjecture becomes implementable, it should return as an editable tutorial or theorem rather than a hidden fixed effect.
